questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Explain why cells stay small in a design brief.
questions.stem: A design brief proposes growing a single cultured cell to 500 micrometres to improve output; explain why the cell would fail before reaching that size.

answer.exemplar: As a cell grows its volume rises faster than its surface area, so the membrane available to exchange materials shrinks relative to the cytoplasm's demand. The cell would starve and waste would accumulate long before 500 micrometres, which is why most cells stay small.

questions.explanation: Volume grows with the cube of radius while membrane area grows with the square, so the ratio falls as a cell enlarges. A large cell cannot exchange nutrients fast enough for its cytoplasm.
questions.hint: Compare volume growth with membrane area growth.
